name: Next-Pay Labor Check
value_proposition: Before the pay period starts, calculate loaded payroll from the posted schedule with visible formulas, flag only against the owner's labor-share target and overtime rule, and re-check against the actual pay run — the Blueprint never edits shifts or payroll.
persona: Owner or manager of a salon, café, clinic, or fitness studio with hourly staff, a posted schedule for the next pay period, and a target for labor as a share of revenue. They only see the true payroll total after the pay run.
problem: Labor cost is known after payday. Overtime and extra shifts are already worked, so the owner cannot change the schedule in time to stay near their labor-to-revenue target.
workflow: 1. The person writes the employer load factor, target labor percentage of revenue, overtime multiplier, overtime flag rule (for example flag if any role has overtime hours > 0), and any minimum coverage rule by role. PERSON DECIDES: the load factor, target, overtime rule, and whether a coverage floor applies.

2. The person exports the next pay period's scheduled hours by role (or by person with names removed), hourly rates by role, overtime hours already on the schedule, and a revenue figure for the same period (POS export or owner estimate labelled as such). PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. Remove employee names, tax IDs, bank details, and other columns the workflow does not need. This is an export review, not a live scheduling, time-clock, POS, or payroll connection.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to upload the file, paste the rows as text, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Next-Pay Labor Check Prompt and their rules from the Labor Target and Overtime Rules Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the schedule and rate rows plus the revenue figure.

5. AI calculates regular pay, overtime at the owner's stated multiplier, and loaded payroll with every formula left visible as text. It calculates loaded payroll as a share of the period's revenue figure. PERSON DECIDES: whether the revenue figure is a POS export or an owner estimate before treating the percentage as actionable.

6. AI flags only when loaded labor percentage is above the owner's target, or when a role's overtime hours exceed the owner's overtime rule. It does not flag a single busy day. It labels CONFIRMED (schedule × rate), OWNER-ENTERED (load factor, target, revenue estimate, overtime rule), CALCULATED (formulas and labor percentage), AI INTERPRETATION (why the gap might exist), and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately.
7. If the person provided a minimum coverage rule, AI lists schedule-edit options that still respect that rule. It does not invent coverage needs. PERSON DECIDES: whether any schedule change happens.

8. The person uses the Schedule Edit Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED dollar and hour against the export row. PERSON DECIDES: edit the next schedule in their own scheduling tool, or change nothing. The Blueprint never changes shifts, pay, or payroll. After the pay run, the person pastes the Actual-Versus-Projected Prompt with the actual payroll total and records the variance.
before: The owner posts next week's schedule from habit, then sees labor as a share of sales only when payroll posts.
after: Before the period starts, the owner sees a loaded payroll figure, whether it exceeds their target share of revenue, which role's hours drive the flag, and a later actual-versus-projected check.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting using a fictional two-role schedule for pay period 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-19, with stylist and front_desk rows (names already removed), employer load 1.20, target labor 40% of revenue, overtime multiplier 1.5, and a flag if any role has overtime hours > 0. Visible formulas show stylist regular, overtime, and loaded payroll; calculated loaded labor is 49.1% of the owner-entered $9,800 revenue figure, above the 40% target, with a stylist overtime flag. AI INTERPRETATION stays separate from the math. A mock post-payroll variance compares projected $4,814.40 to actual $4,960. Confirmed facts, owner-entered inputs, calculated results, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone. Every hour, rate, and dollar is invented. No live scheduling, time-clock, POS, or payroll system is attached.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The schedule export: show the fictional two-role table (stylist: scheduled_hours 128, hourly_rate 22, overtime_hours_in_schedule 4; front_desk: scheduled_hours 64, hourly_rate 18, overtime_hours_in_schedule 0). Show pay_period '2026-04-06 to 2026-04-19', projected_revenue_this_period '9800', employer_load '1.20', target labor '40', overtime multiplier '1.5', and the overtime flag rule 'flag if any role has overtime hours > 0'. Label the table invented. State that no live scheduling, time-clock, POS, or payroll account is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Visible formulas: show the exact heading 'NEXT-PAY LABOR CHECK'. Show CONFIRMED stylist formulas: regular '=124*22' result '2728', overtime '=4*33' result '132', subtotal '2860'. Show CONFIRMED front_desk '=64*18' result '1152'. Show OWNER-ENTERED load '1.20' and CALCULATED loaded payroll '=4012*1.20' result '4814.40'. Show revenue figure '9800' labelled OWNER-ENTERED.

Step 3 of 6 - Target and overtime flags: show CALCULATED loaded labor '=4814.40/9800' result '49.1%' with text that it is above the 40% target. Show an overtime flag for stylist with text containing '4' and 'overtime'. State that a single busy day is not flagged. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'OWNER-ENTERED', 'CALCULATED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone.

Step 4 of 6 - Check the facts: open the stylist CONFIRMED line. A 'Check facts against the export row' button shows three rows (scheduled_hours 128 vs 128, hourly_rate 22 vs 22, overtime_hours_in_schedule 4 vs 4), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Interpretation and later variance: show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'hours' and 'cannot say whether the $9,800 revenue figure is realistic'. Show a mock post-payroll variance: projected '4814.40', actual '4960', variance '=4960-4814.40' result '145.60'. Show the sentence 'Re-check against the actual pay-run total after 2026-04-19.'

Step 6 of 6 - You edit the schedule: state the exact sentences 'You edit the schedule in your own tool. The kit changes nothing.' and 'Do not cut hours that break your minimum coverage.' Explain that the person edits shifts in their own scheduling tool, or decides not to, and that nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All roles, hours, rates, revenue figures, payroll totals, and dates on this page are fictional. No real business data is used, and nothing is connected to a scheduling tool, time clock, POS, payroll provider, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: Next-Pay Labor Check Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one pay period. It covers writing the employer load factor, target labor percentage, overtime multiplier, overtime flag rule, and any minimum coverage rule; exporting scheduled hours by role with names removed, hourly rates, overtime hours already on the schedule, and a same-period revenue figure (POS export or owner estimate labelled as such); checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading; and the rule that this is an export review, not a live scheduling, POS, or payroll connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Next-Pay Labor Check Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that calculates regular pay, overtime at the owner's multiplier, and loaded payroll with every formula visible; calculates loaded labor as a share of the period's revenue figure; flags only against the owner's target and overtime rule; labels CONFIRMED, OWNER-ENTERED, CALCULATED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately; and forbids editing shifts, inventing rates, inventing savings, and treating an owner-estimated revenue figure as a confirmed forecast.

kit_contents.title: Actual-Versus-Projected Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt used only after the pay run. It compares the earlier projected loaded payroll to the owner-entered actual payroll total with a visible variance formula, labels the actual total as OWNER-ENTERED, and forbids inventing the actual figure or editing payroll.

kit_contents.title: Labor Target and Overtime Rules Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets employer load factor, target labor percentage of revenue, overtime multiplier, overtime flag rule, and optional minimum coverage by role. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the Next-Pay Labor Check Prompt. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Loaded Payroll Workbook Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (role, scheduled_hours, regular_hours, overtime_hours, hourly_rate, regular_pay_formula, overtime_pay_formula, role_subtotal, load_factor, loaded_payroll, revenue_figure, labor_pct_formula, labor_pct, target_pct, flag) with the fictional stylist and front_desk demo numbers and visible formula text such as =124*22 and =4012*1.20. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Schedule Edit Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before changing the next schedule. It confirms that every CONFIRMED hour and rate matches the export row, that load factor and revenue figure are labelled OWNER-ENTERED, that formulas stay visible, that flags used only the owner's target and overtime rule, that an owner-estimated revenue figure was not treated as confirmed, that any suggested cut respects the minimum coverage rule, and that the person edits the schedule in their own tool themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Schedule Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional two-role schedule CSV and owner-entered rules used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real payroll or schedule data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling schedule and rate exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove employee names and tax IDs, do not paste bank or payroll login details, do not invent rates or savings, do not treat an owner-estimated revenue figure as a confirmed forecast, do not recommend hour cuts that break minimum coverage or local scheduling rules, and remember that nothing is edited in the scheduling or payroll system automatically. It also states that file upload support differs by plan.

decision_rules: Write NEXT-PAY LABOR CHECK and finish the arithmetic before any schedule-edit suggestion or interpretation.
Use the export's own pay_period dates, not today's date. If the CSV has no pay period, ask the person for it before calculating.
Regular hours for a role equal scheduled_hours minus overtime_hours_in_schedule. Leave every formula visible as text (for example =124*22 and =4*33).
Overtime pay uses only the owner's stated overtime multiplier on the stated hourly rate. Do not invent a multiplier or a different OT rate.
Loaded payroll equals base pay times the owner-entered employer load factor. Leave the formula visible (for example =4012*1.20).

Labor percentage equals loaded payroll divided by the period's revenue figure. Leave the formula visible. Label the revenue figure OWNER-ENTERED when it is an estimate, and do not treat an estimate as a confirmed forecast.
Flag only when calculated loaded labor percentage is above the owner's target, or when a role's overtime_hours_in_schedule exceeds the owner's overtime rule. Do not flag a single busy day.
If a remaining row is missing role, scheduled_hours, or hourly_rate, or the same role appears twice with conflicting rates, do not include it in the totals. List it under NEEDS YOUR CHECK.
Do not invent hours, rates, overtime, load factors, revenue, savings, or ROI. Use only values from the files and rules the person pasted.

Schedule-edit options may be listed only after the calculation and flags. If the person provided a minimum coverage rule, every option must still respect it. If no coverage rule was provided, say so under NEEDS YOUR CHECK and do not invent one.

CONFIRMED means schedule × rate from the export. OWNER-ENTERED means load factor, target, revenue estimate, overtime rule, or actual payroll total. CALCULATED means formula results. AI INTERPRETATION is not a confirmed fact. RECOMMENDED ACTION is never executed by the kit.

On a later run after payday, compare the earlier projected loaded payroll to the owner-entered actual payroll total with a visible variance formula. Do not invent the actual total. If no actual total was provided, say that no actual payroll total was provided.
human_ai_boundary: AI calculates regular pay, overtime, loaded payroll, and labor percentage from the pasted schedule, rates, and owner rules. The person decides the load factor, target, overtime rule, and whether the revenue figure is an estimate or a POS export.
AI flags only against the owner's target and overtime rule. The person decides whether a flag means the next schedule should change.

AI leaves every formula visible and labels CONFIRMED, OWNER-ENTERED, CALCULATED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. The person checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row before treating it as true.
AI may list schedule-edit options that respect a minimum coverage rule the person wrote. The person decides whether any edit happens.

AI never connects to a scheduling tool, time clock, POS, or payroll system, never edits a shift or pay rate, and never uploads the person's files to a third party. The person edits the schedule in their own tool, or decides not to.
AI compares projected loaded payroll to an owner-entered actual total only after the pay run. Only the person records the variance and decides whether to trust the projection next period.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person edits the schedule in their own tool and that the kit changes nothing.

Atlas does not connect to a scheduling tool, time clock, POS, payroll provider, QuickBooks, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings and to remove employee names, tax IDs, bank details, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste payroll login passwords, bank account numbers, Social Security numbers, or full employee names into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.

The kit tells the person not to cut hours that break minimum coverage or local scheduling rules, not to invent rates or savings, and not to treat an owner-estimated revenue figure as a confirmed forecast.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.

The pages contain no invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims, and no price or checkout. The only dollar figures and percentages are the fictional schedule math, owner-entered rules, calculated labor percentage, and the fictional actual-versus-projected variance.
required_data_tools: Scheduling or time-clock export of hours for the next pay period (CSV), names removed
Hourly rates by role (export or owner-entered)
POS or sales figure for the same period, or an owner estimate labelled as such
Owner-entered employer load factor, target labor percentage, overtime multiplier, and overtime flag rule
Optional owner-entered minimum coverage rule by role
Actual payroll total after the pay run (for the variance check)
Spreadsheet (Google Sheets or Excel) so payroll formulas stay visible
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting and the Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

The Premium kit requires requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement for this product. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no Stripe price, checkout, or Buy Premium unless the product is already in PAID_PRODUCTS.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/ai-payroll-forecasting/, components/premium/ai-payroll-forecasting/, and src/lib/premium/ai-payroll-forecasting/. Register the Blueprint in src/lib/blueprints.ts. Do not edit Daily Inbox, Collections product behavior, Stripe, or Production.
e2e/ai-payroll-forecasting/authenticated.spec.ts is read-only once it exists. Do not skip, weaken, or rewrite it. Authenticated QA uses automatic session refresh.
Keyboard accessible, visible labels, no horizontal scrolling at a phone-sized viewport, no console errors.
